title: Donepezil in very early Alzheimer's
description: Donepezil belongs to a group of medicines (acetylcholinesterase inhibitors) used for Alzheimer's dementia. A randomised trial tested it earlier, in people with suspected very early (prodromal) Alzheimer's disease: some took donepezil and others a placebo for a year. The hippocampus shrank in both groups, but about 45% more slowly with donepezil. In this episode brightness stands for the yearly loss of hippocampal volume, not activity: violet means volume lost.
caveat: This is one randomised trial: 216 people at 28 sites in France, with results reported for the 174 who kept to the trial protocol. The participants did not have dementia, and their diagnosis was suspected, not confirmed; the abstract does not say how it was established. The Alzheimer's episode shows activity, while this one shows tissue loss. The hippocampus still shrank with donepezil, only more slowly, and memory and thinking tests did not differ between the groups after a year. A second report by the same study group, apparently from the same trial, found slower shrinkage of the basal forebrain, which is not a separate area in the brain model. These are averages across groups of people, not a picture of any one person's brain. Treatments help many people, not everyone, and in different ways. This is not medical advice: talk to a doctor or therapist about what is right for you.

phases.caption: A different group, over the same year: with donepezil, the hippocampus shrank by about 1.9% a year, 45% more slowly than with placebo.

order.rationale: The two groups were treated at the same time; showing placebo first is only a way of comparing them.

order.rationale: This last part is a summary of what the studies did not find or did not measure, not a later point in time.
